You're going to want to walk around government center, in and around quincy market, through boston common, down by the harbor, along the old I-93 greenway. I recommend the legal harborside restaurant not far from Harpoon, as long as money isn't that important to you.

Off of soldier's field rd you can rent a kayak to go on the charles by the hour, that's nice. Look up concerts at tiny venues using the WZBC concert report.

The museum of science is pretty cool. Or go to the Insitute of Contemporary Art for modern art, or the museum of fine arts for old things.

I think you could miss out on any of those things, though. Coming from the area, it's hard to say I liked getting through to do any touristy stuff. I always ended up driving, and it's the worst out there, second only to trying to park. If you do drive, there is a lot behind the MIT cyclotron that is open at night and pretty obscure that has been a godsend to me many times, vassar st.

The Museum of Fine Arts is always fantastic. Make sure you grab a map, you will get lost. Museum of Science is good, too, if that's more your style.

You could check out the Greenway, downtown, it's one of the greatest things to come to Boston in years and is an absolutely stunning example of embezzlement. The parks and views are nice, too, I guess.

Boston ComicCon is the 12th, and is usually a pretty fun couple of days.

There's a couple nice shops on Newbury St., most of Back Bay is very pretty, actually, definitely worth checking out. Fenway Park is there abouts, too, if you like baseball. Lots of universities there, though (NEU, bits of Harvard, Mass art/design, Wentworth, etc) but if you're lucky, and you keep an eye out or ear open for the green line while on Huntington Ave, you might get to see my absolute favorite sight in all of Boston: oblivious students vs. street level commuter rail.
